players.product: AI server and switch system integration

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration (CFO Mandeep Chawla): 'In the second quarter, three customers each accounted for 10% or more of total revenue, accounting for 32%, 17%, and 14% respectively.'

Segment detail and outlook: Q2 CCS segment margin 8.7% (+40 bps) on operating leverage from significantly higher volumes (CFO). ATS revenue $888M (+8%, above the mid-single-digit outlook), 19% of total revenue, with revenue growth in each ATS business; ATS segment margin 6.3% (+100 bps) — CFO: 'ATS just has the highest margins in its history at 6.3%'. CEO: FY2026 CCS revenue now anticipated to grow by approximately 85%; FY2026 ATS outlook now calls for revenue growth of approximately 10%, accelerating in the second half largely on sequential growth in capital equipment, 'where stronger wafer fab equipment demand tailwinds are anticipated to continue into 2027'. Q3 ATS revenue anticipated up in the mid-teens percentage range (CFO).
quarterly_data.figure: CCS margin 8.7%; ATS $888M (+8%), margin 6.3%; FY26 CCS ~+85%, ATS ~+10%

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance detail (CFO): adjusted EPS $2.88-$3.08 (an increase of $1.40 at the midpoint, 89% growth); adjusted operating margin expected 8.4% at the midpoint of the revenue and EPS ranges (+80 bps); adjusted effective tax rate ~20%. Communications end market expected to grow approximately 60%, 'driven primarily by hyperscaler-led growth in 800G programs, as well as the commencement of mass production ramps in our first 1.6 Terabit programs'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 adj EPS $2.88-$3.08 (+89%); adj op margin 8.4%; communications ~+60%

quarterly_data.signal: Margin drivers (CFO): 'we do believe that we should be able to maintain being around the mid 11s' gross margin through 2026; for 2027 'we have a lot of confidence right now that we will see operating profit expansion for yet another year'. The vast majority of switching programs are HPS (Celestica design, reflected in price); non-HPS business 'is not as margin-rich as HPS products'. Factories 'are running at a high level of utilization. It is not by accident. It is intentional', with double-digit productivity across the majority of sites. On CCS growth: 'CCS is going to be growing close to 85% year-over-year. We are going to see a similar level of growth next year.'
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin around the mid 11s through 2026; operating profit expansion expected in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue model and customer terms (CFO): 'the vast majority of our networking has the silicon included, and the vast majority of our compute does not have the silicon included. Those dynamics are really holding as we go into next year.' 'In some cases, we have binding forecasts that go out 12-18 months in order to secure the materials'; customers cover specialized equipment or non-recurring expenses, Celestica the majority of the rest — 'we're not a bank, so we don't go and fund our customers' ability to grow' — and 'We have no concerns across our customer base at this time.'
quarterly_data.figure: binding forecasts out 12-18 months in some cases

quarterly_data.signal: Demand visibility (Q&A): CFO: 'We're having demand conversations in 2027, for 2028, and in some cases even for 2029'; what changed in the last three to six months is that materials had to be ordered for next year, and 'With those orders now in place, it gives us just that one extra level of confidence'. CEO: base demand for 800G programs 'has also just dramatically increased for 2027'; after a dynamic start to the year, customers' demand signals 'normalized and strengthened', and customers 'continue to want more than the supply chain could supply, that is, again, not perishable demand'; 'the unprecedented levels of demand visibility is enabled by extended lead times'. On 2027: 'We're not placing a ceiling on the upside at this time'.
quarterly_data.figure: demand conversations out to 2028-2029; materials orders for 2027 in place

quarterly_data.signal: Capex, working capital and footprint (CFO): Q2 capital expenditures $264M, approximately 5.6% of revenue vs 1.1% in the prior-year quarter, intended to support growth from currently ramping and awarded programs; Q2 free cash flow $147M ($285M year-to-date); inventory $3.4B (+$0.7B sequentially) to support upcoming CCS program ramps; cash cycle 47 days. Capacity additions are 'quite global': Thailand (a flagship location supporting a number of the highest-growth customers), expansions in Japan at customers' request including 'moving some switching business into Japan', Richardson TX (existing footprint expanding) and Fort Worth TX (new capacity coming online now and more next year); 'our customers right now are looking for an equal amount of growth in Asia as well as in the United States.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex $264M (~5.6% of revenue); FCF $147M; inventory $3.4B; cash cycle 47 days

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up beyond Helios and the OpenAI rack (CEO): 'we have numerous engagements and discussions with folks to go into scale up. Scale up for us really started with 1.6T, as we continue to win awards for integrated rack systems, we expect this to be a huge opportunity for us.' CEO on differentiation: 'Some people do design, some people do manufacturing. We do both'; customers value the design-to-ramp transition (CFO).
